title: Rosemary roast potatoes
intro: Crisp outside, fluffy inside, with whole garlic cloves and rosemary.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 220 °C. Peel the potatoes and cut into 3 cm chunks.

airfryer.t: Peel the potatoes and cut into 3 cm chunks.

steps.t: Parboil in salted water for 5 minutes, drain and shake in the colander to rough up the edges.
steps.label: Potatoes

steps.t: Toss on a baking tray with the oil, rosemary, crushed garlic and salt, in a single layer.
Roast for 40 minutes, turning halfway, until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Roast

airfryer.t: Air-fry at 200 °C for 25 minutes, shaking the basket every 8 minutes.

steps.t: Season with pepper and serve hot.

tips.t: Shaking them in the colander roughs up the edges, which turn into a crunchy crust.
Add a red onion cut into wedges halfway through.
Crisp leftovers in a pan or fold them into a frittata.

title: Patatas bravas
intro: Twice-fried, extra-crisp potatoes with a spicy smoked paprika sauce.

steps.t: Peel the potatoes, cut into rough 3 cm chunks, rinse and dry well.
Fry in the oil at 140 °C for 10 minutes, until tender but still pale; drain.
steps.label: First fry

airfryer.t: Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp oil and air-fry at 200 °C for 20 minutes, shaking now and then.

oven.t: Toss the potatoes with 2 tbsp oil and roast at 220 °C for 35 minutes, turning halfway.

steps.t: Meanwhile, warm the garlic in 2 tbsp oil, take off the heat, stir in paprika and cayenne, then passata, vinegar, sugar and salt; simmer 10 minutes.
steps.label: Sauce

steps.t: Heat the oil to 180 °C and fry the potatoes again for 4 minutes, until golden and crisp.
steps.label: Crisp

airfryer.t: Take the potatoes out when golden and crisp.

oven.t: Take the potatoes out when golden and crisp.

steps.t: Drain, salt and serve with the bravas sauce on top.

tips.t: The double fry is the secret: the first cooks the inside, the second builds the crust.
For quick alioli, mix mayonnaise with 1 grated garlic clove and serve alongside.

title: Swabian potato salad
intro: Sliced potatoes soak up hot stock and vinegar: creamy with no mayo.

steps.t: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 25 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
steps.label: Potatoes

pressure.t: Cook the unpeeled potatoes in the pressure cooker with 250 ml water for 10 minutes at high pressure.

steps.t: Meanwhile, chop the onion and bring it to a boil in the stock (store-bought is fine) with vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper.
Drain the potatoes, peel them while hot and slice 5 mm thick into a bowl.
Pour over the boiling stock, mix gently and let it soak for 20 minutes, stirring a couple of times.
steps.label: Soak

steps.t: Add the oil and stir until creamy; adjust the seasoning and finish with chives.

tips.t: Boiling stock on still-hot potatoes is everything: they absorb it and turn creamy.
Classic with sausages, meatballs or Wiener schnitzel.
Add thinly sliced cucumber or crisp-fried bacon.

title: Gratin dauphinois
intro: Sliced potatoes baked slowly in milk and cream under a golden crust.

steps.t: Heat the oven to 160 °C. Rub a baking dish with the cut garlic and butter it.
Peel the potatoes and slice them 3 mm thick, without rinsing: the starch thickens the cream.
Bring the milk and cream to a simmer with grated garlic, nutmeg, salt and pepper; add the potatoes and cook 10 minutes, stirring gently.
steps.label: Cream

steps.t: Pour everything into the dish and level the top.
Bake for 1 hour 15 minutes, until golden on top and a knife slides through easily.
steps.label: Bake

steps.t: Let it rest for 15 minutes before serving.
steps.label: Rest

tips.t: Simmering the potatoes in the milk and cream first shortens baking and makes it creamier.
Perfect with roast leg of lamb or roast beef.
Cut leftovers into squares when cold and reheat at 180 °C for 15 minutes.
